headline: Arteta's new Arsenal deal, Real Madrid-La Liga feud escalates
paragraphs: Mikel Arteta has agreed a new contract to stay at Arsenal, with BBC Sport and Sky Sports both reporting the deal independently — separate newsrooms, not one story recycled. BBC Sport describes it as an "improved new contract" with the Premier League champions; Sky Sports says it extends his stay. This is settled, on-the-record news, not a rumour: Arteta's immediate future at Arsenal is resolved, in contrast to most of the day's other reporting.

Real Madrid's row with La Liga president Javier Tebas escalated after Sunday's Madrid derby defeat. Tebas said claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid were like "living in another galaxy," per BBC Sport; Real Madrid responded by calling his comments "intolerable" and demanding his removal, according to the Guardian. Two separate outlets are covering the same feud from opposite sides — this is a live dispute, not a resolved one, and each side blames the other.

Elsewhere the six clubs saw only single-source, unconfirmed reporting. FourFourTwo says Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres, yet to start in the league this season, is in talks over an "expensive" departure; Transfermarkt separately lists Arsenal as watching Maximilian Beier and Liverpool as eyeing Lamine Camara. Neither report is corroborated elsewhere in today's feed. The one settled fact: per Opta, Erling Haaland's goal against Sunderland means he has now scored against all 25 Premier League clubs he has faced.
